column4: Engineers designed a banana‑shaped satellite that peels off data as it circles Earth, proving that even fruit can be a high‑tech spy.
column5: The banana wanted a career in aerospace, so it trained to become a peel‑orbiting satellite—always staying on the same wavelength and never slipping up.

column4: I walked into the kitchen and saw an angry teacup leading a protest against sugar, chanting, "No more sweet talk!" while the mug filed a restraining order.
column5: An angry coworker is like a teacup left on the stove: you can see the steam rising, you know it’s about to boil over, but you still keep sipping the gossip.

column4: In the nebula café, the cosmic toaster floated by, toasting bread with supernova heat while the crumbs formed brand‑new constellations.
column5: My therapist says I’m a cosmic toaster—full of potential inside, but everyone only ever sees the browned exterior.

column4: I woke up to find a sleepy volcano snoring on my roof, puffing out soft ash clouds like pillow‑smoke.
column5: Why did the volcano feel sleepy? Because it couldn't stop counting lava‑sheep before its next eruption.

column4: Need a night‑shift guard? Hire a neon hamster: it scurries through dark hallways, its glowing fur acting like a living exit sign that never takes a coffee break.
column5: I walked into a club where a neon hamster was DJing; every scratch on the record made the lights flicker like a hamster wheel on a caffeine binge.

column4: Why was the penguin so awkward at the party? Because every time it tried to break the ice, it slipped on its own tuxedo!
column5: Introducing the new yoga pose: the Awkward Penguin, where you balance on one foot while flapping your arms like you’re trying to hail a taxi.

column4: I tried to plug my dinner into the wall—turns out electric spaghetti just gives you a shocking al dente.
column5: The new Italian restaurant offers a ‘Volt‑agnese’—a sauce so electric that your spaghetti literally glows in the dark.

column4: I tuned into a desert soap opera where the cactus gave a dramatic soliloquy about feeling misunderstood, while the tumbleweeds offered a standing ovation.
column5: Why did the cactus audition for the play? It heard the part was highly dramatic and loved the idea of delivering a prickly monologue.

column4: A confused astronaut tried filing his taxes with a meteor and was told you can’t claim a shooting star as a dependent.
column5: The confused astronaut kept looking for the space bar, but all he found were actual bars floating in zero‑gravity.

column4: Imagine a tornado made of rubber: it spins forever, every gust ends with a squeak, and the only debris is over‑inflated balloon animals.
column5: A rubber duck entered a tornado and emerged as a 'twist‑quacker'—a squeaky cyclone that leaves a trail of bubbles wherever it lands.

column4: My diet includes an invisible taco: I can see I’m not eating it, yet my stomach still hears the satisfying crunch.
column5: Scientists tried to create an invisible taco for stealth meals, but the only thing it concealed was the calories, not the crunch.

column4: A therapist once prescribed a sarcastic dolphin for my anxiety; every session ended with it flippantly saying, "Just keep swimming, or don’t—your call," while handing me a kelp‑shaped stress ball.
column5: In the underwater courtroom, the sarcastic dolphin acted as judge, flipping his flippers and declaring, "I’m sorry, your case is…flippin’ adorable, but I’m too busy making bubbles."

column4: I bought a haunted calculator.  It still works, but it keeps giving me 666 for everything.
column5: I asked my haunted calculator how many cups of sugar for a ghost cake, and it replied “π‑spirit”—now I’m baking with irrational scares.

column4: The weather report said 'spicy clouds incoming,' which turned out to be just a hot‑air balloon scented with jalapeño.
column5: In the sky’s kitchen, clouds simmer in a cauldron of chili oil, so every lightning bolt arrives with a side of fire‑breathing salsa.

column4: When the librarian turned the reading room into a disco, the Dewey Decimal System became a dance floor: 500s were funky physics, 800s were smooth opera, and the only fine was a missed dance step.
column5: The librarian opened a disco because she heard the stacks needed a good "record" spin, and now overdue notices come with glittery 12‑inch sleeves.

column4: My lonely robot asked for a friend, so I gave it a charging cable—now it’s constantly surrounded by ‘current’ companions.
column5: Ever notice how a lonely robot is the only coworker who never steals your lunch, because it can’t even open the fridge without a firmware update?

column4: I walked into a forest and saw a caffeinated squirrel conducting a rave for the acorns, complete with tiny turntables and jittery beats.
column5: I can't believe I got fired just because of a typo! I meant to write: "I will not steal a tree." Instead I wrote: "I will not steal a caffeinated squirrel."

column4: My brain sometimes feels like a confused mailbox; thoughts pile up, I flag them for later, and the only delivery I get is a “you’ve got mail” notification from my own head.
column5: In an alternate universe a confused mailbox is a therapist—drop a letter and it replies, “Tell me why you’re feeling so stamped.”
